Fifteen comments

The Devils of Dublin

Here you go Josh. I pulled a version of this off the wooden flute tune data base last fall and tweaked the ornamentation to fit my style. Nice tune. You can make the melody flow more by replacing some of the rolls with strings of notes, so the A~F3 in the first half could be played AFDF instead, etc.

↳ Posted by Will Harmon on February 9th, 2002.

YOU’RE MY HERO!!!

↳ Posted by Josh Kane on February 9th, 2002.

Well, who’d have thought that the Merry Blacksmith would be a manifestation of the Dark Forces? This tune appears to be a version of the Merry Blacksmith, and not in the least diabolical - quite the opposite.

↳ Posted by CreadurMawnOrganig on February 12th, 2002.

I heard this at my local session and I was told that it was the Michael Coleman version of the Merry Blacksmith. I didn’t realise it had a different name.

↳ Posted by Dr. Dow on November 21st, 2004.

The Connacht Reel

While doing a search on tunepal.org, I fell on the above 4th setting as a possible match in addition to Devils of Dublin proposition. It is named The Connacht Reel from the Book “Treoir”. I don’t remember from which database it is, so thanks to the original transcriptor.

↳ Posted by didier on June 19th, 2015.

Devils Of Dublin, X:5

Pieced together from Comb Your Hair And Curl It By Catherine McEvoy, Caoimhín Ó Raghallaigh, Mícheál Ó Raghallaigh

https://thesession.org/recordings/3657

They are all really playing quite different stuff, it’s amazing, but obviously hard to transcribe a decent version which captures the overall feel… this is what I’ve ended up with.

↳ Posted by jamesa on March 11th, 2022.

Devils Of Dublin, X:6

Donogh Hennessy’s setting of Lunasa’s version from ‘Otherworld’ as per ‘Lunasa The Music 1996-2001’. I’ve added some ~’s and condensed the second part.

↳ Posted by Edgar Bolton on September 21st, 2022.

Devils Of Dublin, X:7

I believe this is a more or less accurate transcription of what Catherine McEvoy is doing on her recording with Felix Dolan, and some of these choices also appear on “Comb Your Hair and Curl It”.

↳ Posted by AdamM on October 15th, 2023.

Re: Devils Of Dublin - a stomping session version from 2011

There’s stomping version of this from an “impromptu session of music in the old style led by Josephine [Keegan] herself”. 2011. It’s the real deal.
https://www.itma.ie/playlists/josephine-keegan/?track=3
There’s a lot of gold out there on itma.

↳ Posted by GoPlayer on July 10th, 2024.

Re: Devils Of Dublin AKA the Connacht

I found a very nice recording of this on ITMA Denis Ryan and Cathal McConnell, under the name of the Connacht reel. I updated the AKA section here with that name, maybe I shouldn’t have?

https://www.itma.ie/playlists/michael-mcnamara-sound-collection-playlist/?track=17
Denis Ryan, fiddle; Cathal McConnell, flute
The Connacht; Cooley’s; The Bucks of Oranmore

(A warning for ITMA links: you have to click on the tune in the playlist once the page is displayed rather than simply clicking on play.)

I’m very fond of this reel. There’s a lot of scope for variation in it I think.

↳ Posted by GoPlayer on February 15th, 2026.
